'''Axel Sophus Guldberg''' (2 November 1838 – 28 February 1913) was a [[Norwegian mathematician]].<ref name="snl">{{cite encyclopedia |title=Axel Sophus Guldberg |url=https://snl.no/Axel_Sophus_Guldberg |encyclopedia=[[Store norske leksikon|SNL]] |date=30 November 2021 |access-date=7 September 2022 |language=nb}}</ref><ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last1=Blangstrup |first1=Christian |title=Guldberg, 1. Axel Sophus |date=1915–30 |encyclopedia=[[Salmonsens Konversationsleksikon]] |page=393 |edition=2 |url=https://runeberg.org/salmonsen/2/10/0413.html |access-date=13 October 2022 |language=da}}</ref><ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title=Guldberg, 3. Axel Sofus |date=1909 |encyclopedia=[[Nordisk familjebok]] |page=591 |edition=2 |url=https://runeberg.org/nfbj/0324.html |access-date=13 October 2022 |language=sv}}</ref>

==Biography==
Born in Christiania (now called Oslo), Guldberg was the second oldest out of 11 siblings.<ref name="nbl">{{cite encyclopedia |last1=Birkeland |first1=Bent |title=Axel Guldberg |url=https://nbl.snl.no/Axel_Guldberg |encyclopedia=[[Norsk biografisk leksikon|NBL]] |date=29 June 2022 |access-date=7 September 2022 |language=nb}}</ref> He and his siblings were initially homeschooled, but he and his older brother, [[Cato Maximilian Guldberg]], later began going to school in [[Fredrikstad]], where they lived together with relatives.<ref name="nbl" /> He completed his [[examen artium]] in 1856,<ref name="nbl" /> [[cand.real.]] in 1863<ref name="nbl" /> and [[dr.philos.]] in 1867.<ref name="snl" /><ref name="nbl" />

In 1863, he was an [[adjunct professor]] in [[Drammen]].<ref name="nbl" /> From 1864 to 1865, he studied mathematics in Germany and France, while simultaneously on his honeymoon.<ref name="nbl" /> In 1865, Guldberg became a [[Rector (academia)|rector]] in [[Stavanger]].<ref name="snl" /><ref name="nbl" /> The same year, he began teaching mathematics at the [[Norwegian Military Academy]] until 1899.<ref name="snl" /><ref name="nbl" />

He was an important figure in the insurance industry.<ref name="snl" /><ref name="nbl" /> He also served in the Norwegian [[law commission]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Langeland |first1=Nils Rune |editor1-last=Ulvund |editor1-first=Frode |title=Aksjelova av 1910 |journal=Historisk Tidsskrift |date=16 March 2021 |volume=100 |issue=1 |pages=22–35 |trans-title=The Shares Act of 1910 |publisher=[[Universitetsforlaget]] |doi=10.18261/issn.1504-2944-2021-01-03 |s2cid=233650444 |language=nn|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In 1866, he had a son, [[Alf Victor Guldberg]], with his wife, Fredrikke Borchsenius.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last1=Steenstrup |first1=Bjørn |title=GULDBERG Alf Victor Emanuel |date=1930 |encyclopedia=[[Hvem er hvem?]] |page=152 |edition=2 |url=https://runeberg.org/hvemerhvem/1930/0152.html |access-date=16 October 2022}}</ref>
